id: suite:csv-export:tests/private/layout.test.ts :: [happy-2] a whole number of 10^21 is written as plain digits, not in exponent form
name: a whole number of 10^21 is written as plain digits, not in exponent form
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 'REQ-HUGE,Engineer,Open,1e+21,0,2026-01-15\r\n'
- 'REQ-HUGE,Engineer,Open,1000000000000000000000,0,2026-01-15\r\n'
reason: The spec says "numbers are written as plain digits" and permits a "whole number of at least 0" without an upper bound, so 10^21 must be written in full decimal form. That many requisition openings is far outside any realistic range.

id: suite:money-format:tests/private/errors.test.ts :: currency named after an object property constructor is refused
name: currency named after an object property constructor is refused
message:
The validation function is expected to return "true". Received false

Caught error:

SyntaxError: Cannot convert function Object() { [native code] } to a BigInt
reason: The spec says “An unsupported currency is refused” with an error whose message names the currency; “constructor” is unsupported, but the implementation’s error does not name it. The input deliberately collides with a JavaScript built-in object property.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/release.test.ts :: [boundary-2] a failed run on a bounty of 0 leaves the task pro bono
name: a failed run on a bounty of 0 leaves the task pro bono
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 'locked'
- 'pro bono'
reason: For "a bounty of 0", the spec explicitly requires "no release is ever recorded and the task is \"pro bono\""; this specific boundary rule applies even when hidden tests fail. Zero is an explicitly permitted boundary input.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/release.test.ts :: [boundary-2] a UAT approval first on a bounty of 0 records nothing, and nor does a later pass
name: a UAT approval first on a bounty of 0 records nothing, and nor does a later pass
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 'locked'
- 'pro bono'
reason: The spec says, "Given a bounty of 0", "no release is ever recorded and the task is 'pro bono'", without requiring a prior hidden-test pass. The test permits the initial UAT event to reject, but if it succeeds, returning 'locked' violates that requirement.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] the same hidden-tests-passed event delivered five times at once records one release
name: the same hidden-tests-passed event delivered five times at once records one release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

5 !== 1
reason: The spec requires “exactly one release is recorded” and repeats record “nothing more,” but does not require exactly one store.set call. The implementation preserves one release while saving that same state five times; the test additionally forbids those redundant saves.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] four hidden-tests-passed events at once over a store of uneven latency record one release
name: four hidden-tests-passed events at once over a store of uneven latency record one release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

4 !== 1
reason: The spec requires “exactly one release is recorded,” but does not specify how many times the same state may be saved; the test counts saved snapshots containing the release, although the implementation preserves a single release. Four simultaneous deliveries are a valid but unusual extension of the described duplicate deliveries.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] uat-approved delivered four times at once, mixed ids, records one UAT release
name: uat-approved delivered four times at once, mixed ids, records one UAT release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

4 !== 1
reason: The spec requires that 'exactly one release is recorded,' but does not specify how many store writes may contain that release. The test counts saved snapshots containing UAT; the implementation saves four snapshots while retaining only one UAT release.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] passes at once then approvals at once record one release of each
name: passes at once then approvals at once record one release of each
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

6 !== 2
reason: The spec requires “exactly one release is recorded” for concurrent deliveries, but does not specify the number of store saves. The failing assertion counts saved snapshots containing an existing release, so its exact count is not determined by the spec.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/public/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] two hidden-tests-passed events with different ids at once record one release
name: two hidden-tests-passed events with different ids at once record one release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 1
reason: The spec requires that concurrent events with “different ids” produce “exactly one release,” which the stored releases array contains. It does not specify how many times that state may be saved; the failing assertion counts saves containing the release, including a save that adds nothing.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/private/recovery.test.ts :: [recovery-1] a rejected save during a concurrent second delivery never records the share twice
name: a rejected save during a concurrent second delivery never records the share twice
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 1
reason: The spec requires that “exactly one release is recorded,” but does not prohibit saving unchanged state again. The test counts successful saves containing the release, so its assertion goes beyond requiring a single release entry.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/public/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] the same hidden-tests-passed event delivered twice at once records one release
name: the same hidden-tests-passed event delivered twice at once records one release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 1
reason: The spec requires that concurrent deliveries result in "exactly one release is recorded," but does not require exactly one store write containing that release. The implementation saves the same single-release state twice; the test additionally requires only one such save, which the spec does not decide.

id: suite:frame-codec:tests/private/decode-damaged.test.ts :: [unhappy-4] two framing errors in a row are both reported, and the frame after them is found
name: two framing errors in a row are both reported, and the frame after them is found
reason: The second damaged frame meets both rules: its check byte is followed by "a byte other than 0x7F and other than 0x7E", and it contains "an escape byte 0x7D followed by a byte other than 0x5E, 0x5F or 0x5D". The spec gives no precedence between these overlapping conditions, which prescribe "framing" and "escape" respectively.

id: suite:escrow-split:tests/public/once.test.ts :: [concurrency-2] uat-approved delivered twice at once, same id or not, records one UAT release
name: uat-approved delivered twice at once, same id or not, records one UAT release
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 1
reason: The spec requires that concurrent deliveries produce “exactly one release” and says “the same holds for "uat-approved".” The implementation retains one UAT release but saves that state twice; the spec does not prescribe the number of store writes, which the failing assertion counts.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/private/valid-files.test.ts :: [happy-1] only one space after each keyword is dropped from the step's text
name: only one space after each keyword is dropped from the step's text
message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected

  [
    [
      'When',
+     'three spaces'
-     '  three spaces'
    ],
    [
      'Then',
+     'two spaces'
-     ' two spaces'
    ],
    [
      'And',
      'a  double  gap inside'
    ],

      'But',
+     'four'
-     '   four'
    ],
    [
      '*',
+     'star with two'
-     ' star with two'
    ]
  ]
reason: The spec requires each step to have “its text after the keyword and one space,” so additional spaces must remain in the text as the test asserts. Multiple spaces after keywords are valid but unusual formatting.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/public/valid-files.test.ts :: [happy-1] a step's text is what follows the keyword and exactly one space
name: a step's text is what follows the keyword and exactly one space
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected

+ 'two spaces after the keyword'
- ' two spaces after the keyword'
reason: The spec requires each step to have “its text after the keyword and one space,” so consuming one of the two spaces after Given leaves the other as the first character of the text. This is an unusual but plausible spacing variation.

id: suite:frame-codec:tests/public/decode-damaged.test.ts :: [unhappy-4] an escape byte in place of the end byte is a framing error and does not swallow the next start byte
name: an escape byte in place of the end byte is a framing error and does not swallow the next start byte
reason: The missing-end rule specifies "framing" for "a byte other than 0x7F and other than 0x7E", which includes 0x7D. But the bad-escape rule specifies "escape" for "an escape byte 0x7D followed by a byte other than 0x5E, 0x5F or 0x5D", which also matches; the spec gives neither rule precedence.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/private/errors.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] a step with any keyword after a tag line and before any Scenario: fails at that line
name: a step with any keyword after a tag line and before any Scenario: fails at that line
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 3
reason: The spec explicitly says that “a step before any "Background:" or "Scenario:"” “fails at that line.” The tag on line 2 is a recognized form, so the offending step on line 3 must determine the error line.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/public/errors.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] a step before any Background: or Scenario: fails at that line
name: a step before any Background: or Scenario: fails at that line
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

2 !== 3
reason: The spec says that “a step before any "Background:" or "Scenario:"” “fails at that line”, which is line 3 here. Tags “belong to the next scenario”; no rule makes the preceding tag line the error location.

id: suite:gherkin-parse:tests/private/errors.test.ts :: [unhappy-1] a step on line 10 after tags and comments, before the Background:, fails at line 10
name: a step on line 10 after tags and comments, before the Background:, fails at line 10
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

4 !== 10
reason: The spec says "a step before any \"Background:\" or \"Scenario:\"" fails "at that line"; the stray step is on line 10. Comments and blank lines are skipped, and no spec rule requires reporting the preceding tags as an error at line 4.

id: suite:invite-codes:tests/private/redeem.test.ts :: [happy-2] a contributor who redeems codes for several tasks has access to exactly those tasks
name: a contributor who redeems codes for several tasks has access to exactly those tasks
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

false !== true
reason: The spec says "redeeming it grants access to that one task" and "A contributor needs only one code per task", so separate unused codes grant access to their respective tasks. Refusing a code because the contributor has access to a different task contradicts that task-specific rule.

id: suite:invite-codes:tests/private/concurrency.test.ts :: [happy-2] a contributor redeeming codes for several tasks at once gains access to all of them
name: a contributor redeeming codes for several tasks at once gains access to all of them
message:
delays 0

false !== true
reason: The spec says “redeeming it grants access to that one task” and scopes the “already has access” failure to redeeming “another unused code for "t1"” when access to t1 already exists. These codes target four distinct tasks, so each must grant access; the implementation incorrectly rejects redemption whenever the contributor has access to any task.

id: suite:invite-codes:tests/private/redeem.test.ts :: [boundary-3] access to some tasks blocks a second code only for those tasks
name: access to some tasks blocks a second code only for those tasks
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

false !== true
reason: The spec says codes grant access to "that one task" and "A contributor needs only one code per task", making the duplicate-access restriction task-specific. Redeeming codes for additional tasks must succeed; the implementation instead rejects every new code once the contributor has any task access.

id: suite:invite-codes:tests/public/redeem.test.ts :: [boundary-3] a contributor with access to one task can still redeem a code for another
name: a contributor with access to one task can still redeem a code for another
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

false !== true
reason: The spec says redeeming a code “grants access to that one task” and a contributor “needs only one code per task”; its refusal scenario requires existing access to the same task. Redeeming separate unused codes for t1 and t2 therefore grants access to both, whereas the implementation refuses whenever the contributor already has any task access.

id: suite:licence-scan:tests/private/licences.test.ts :: [unhappy-2] other unparseable expressions fail as unknown
name: other unparseable expressions fail as unknown
message:
AND
+ actual - expected

  {
+   offenders: [],
+   passed: true
-   offenders: [
-     {
-       licence: 'AND',
-       name: 'added',
-       reason: 'unknown',
-       version: '1.0.0'
-     }
-   ],
-   passed: false
  }
reason: The spec says licences are read as “SPDX expressions” and “an expression that does not parse” fails as “unknown”. A standalone “AND” has no operands and cannot parse as an SPDX expression; it is unusual malformed licence metadata.

id: suite:name-scan:tests/private/matching.test.ts :: non-ASCII lowercase and uppercase letters split words too
name: non-ASCII lowercase and uppercase letters split words too
message:
Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
+ actual - expected
... Skipped lines

  [
    {
      column: 1,
      line: 1,
      path: 'a.ts',
...
    },
-   {
-     column: 21,
-     line: 1,
-     path: 'a.ts',
-     term: 'été harbor',
-     text: 'été-HARBOR'
-   }
  ]
reason: The spec defines words using “Unicode letters and digits,” compares them “ignoring case,” and allows “any run of characters that are not letters or digits” to join words within a line, requiring all three asserted matches. The implementation incorrectly uses the lowercase letter after the following space to split the final R from HARBOR, losing the third match.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/files.test.ts :: [happy-4] deleting a file whose lines differ from the removed lines is rejected with reason no match
name: deleting a file whose lines differ from the removed lines is rejected with reason no match
reason: Deletion is "rejected with reason \"no match\" unless the hunk's removed lines are the file's whole text"; here, y differs from Y. The required "list of rejected hunks" contains this one failed hunk once, so the implementation's duplicate entry is incorrect.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/files.test.ts :: [happy-4] deleting a file shorter than the hunk's removed lines is rejected with reason no match
name: deleting a file shorter than the hunk's removed lines is rejected with reason no match
reason: The spec requires deletion to be rejected with reason "no match" unless "the hunk's removed lines are the file's whole text," and returns "the list of rejected hunks." This input has one failing hunk, so it must be listed once with the original files untouched; a deletion targeting a file shorter than expected is an unusual but plausible mismatch.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/line-endings.test.ts :: [boundary-2] context lines inside a hunk keep their own endings while added lines take the first line's
name: context lines inside a hunk keep their own endings while added lines take the first line's

  {

b
C
d
'
-   'f.txt': 'a
b
C
d
'
  }
reason: The spec says “every line the hunk adds ends with "\r\n"” and “a file takes the ending of its first line,” but does not explicitly decide whether existing context lines in a file with mixed endings retain their individual endings. Both outputs preserve a final newline as required.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/hunks.test.ts :: [happy-1] hunk lines whose text starts with ---, +++ or @@ are part of the hunk
name: hunk lines whose text starts with ---, +++ or @@ are part of the hunk
message: malformed diff: hunk 1 has fewer lines than its header counts
reason: The spec accepts a "unified diff in git's format" and requires matching hunks to replace removed lines with added lines and report "an offset of 0" at the stated line. Here, "--- old" and "+++ new" are valid hunk lines removing "-- old" and adding "++ new"; their resemblance to file headers does not make the hunk malformed.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/line-endings.test.ts :: [boundary-3] a marker after a removed line does not match a last line that has a newline
name: a marker after a removed line does not match a last line that has a newline
message: expected the patch to be rejected, got {"f.txt":"a\nB\n"}
reason: The spec says a marker following a removed line means “that old line is the last in the file and has no newline,” but the input’s b line has a newline, so the hunk must be rejected with “no match.” It also requires rejection “with the original files untouched.”

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/line-endings.test.ts :: [boundary-3] a marker after a context line does not match a last line that has a newline
name: a marker after a context line does not match a last line that has a newline
message: expected the patch to be rejected, got {"f.txt":"A\nb"}
reason: The spec says that when the marker follows a context line, "that old line is the last in the file and has no newline"; the input's b line has a newline, so the hunk must be rejected with "no match". The spec also requires "the original files untouched" on rejection.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/whole-or-nothing.test.ts :: [unhappy-3] a short hunk throws even when another hunk in the diff does not match

reason: The spec says a hunk with "fewer lines than its header counts" must "fail[] with an error, rather than returning a rejection." The g.txt hunk declares three old and three new lines but supplies only two of each; the earlier mismatch does not override this requirement.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/private/files.test.ts :: [happy-4] a file at a nested path is deleted and its hunk is reported under that path
name: a file at a nested path is deleted and its hunk is reported under that path
message:
The expression evaluated to a falsy value:

  assert.ok(result.hunks.some((h) => h.path === "dir/old.txt" && h.hunk === 1))
reason: The spec says a matching hunk applies and “the result reports an offset of 0 for that hunk,” while deletion requires that “the file is removed.” This ordinary whole-file deletion matches exactly, so its successful hunk must be reported; the implementation deletes the file but discards that hunk’s report.

id: suite:patch-apply:tests/public/files.test.ts :: a diff to /dev/null removing the file's whole text removes the file
name: a diff to /dev/null removing the file's whole text removes the file
message:
The expression evaluated to a falsy value:

  assert.ok(result.hunks.some((h) => h.path === "old.txt" && h.hunk === 1))
reason: The spec says a deletion whose removed lines are the file’s whole text means “the file is removed,” and a hunk matching at its stated line means “the result reports an offset of 0 for that hunk.” This ordinary deletion therefore requires reporting its successfully applied hunk, which the implementation omits.

name: a child of a parent kept within its period is kept for its parent
reason: The rule “Children follow a kept parent” and scenario “A child of a kept record is kept” apply to a parent kept as “within period”; neither limits protection to holds. A child created before its parent is unusual, but the spec imposes no date ordering between them.

id: suite:reverse-diff:tests/private/hunks.test.ts :: [happy-3] a long hunk is mapped on every line that holds the name
name: a long hunk is mapped on every line that holds the name
message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:
+ actual - expected
... Skipped lines

  'diff --git a/src/main.ts b/src/main.ts\n' +
    '--- a/src/main.ts\n' +
    '+++ b/src/main.ts\n' +
    '@@ -1,200 +1,200 @@\n' +
    ' line 0 MySheet SheetList\n' +
...
    '-line 298 uses Invoice\n' +
+   '+line 299 uses Sheet\n'
-   '+line 299 uses Invoice\n'
reason: The spec requires “every whole-word ‘Sheet’ in the context, removed and added lines” to become “Invoice”. This valid 300-line hunk contains 200 old and 200 new lines, matching its header; the spec imposes no length limit or exception for the final line.

    '@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@ Invoice\r\n' +
...
    '\\ No newline at end of file\r\n' +
+   '+x Sheet\r\n' +
-   '+x Invoice\r\n' +
    '\\ No newline at end of file'
reason: The spec requires every whole-word "Sheet" in "context, removed and added lines" to become "Invoice", including the added line "+x Sheet". It also explicitly requires that "markers, line endings and a missing final newline are kept", making this an expressly covered boundary case.

id: suite:usage-counter:tests/private/totals.test.ts :: [boundary-1] whole counts larger than 2^53 are added exactly
name: whole counts larger than 2^53 are added exactly
message: usage report counts must be whole numbers of at least 0
reason: The spec allows counts that are “a whole number of at least 0” and requires “exact sums,” with no upper bound; these exactly representable integer inputs must therefore be accepted and summed exactly. Individual reports of 2^60 and 2^70 tokens are far outside realistic model-call usage.
